traits.flower_symmetry.note: Brenan's Flora of Tropical East Africa account of Mimosoideae (1959): subfamily (p. 1) flowers usually small or very small and regular; Acacia (p. 49), which then held Vachellia: flowers in spikes, spike-like racemes or round heads, stamens many (35 to about 215 in the East African species), free; the native species almost all armed. Abrams (vol. 2, 1944, p. 475) for Acacia: flowers small, usually yellow, in heads or spikes, stamens many, exserted.

traits.stamens.note: Brenan's Flora of Tropical East Africa account of Mimosoideae (1959): subfamily (p. 1) flowers usually small or very small and regular; Acacia (p. 49), which then held Vachellia: flowers in spikes, spike-like racemes or round heads, stamens many (35 to about 215 in the East African species), free; the native species almost all armed. Abrams (vol. 2, 1944, p. 475) for Acacia: flowers small, usually yellow, in heads or spikes, stamens many, exserted. The range is for Acacia in the old wide sense in East Africa; no figure for Vachellia alone.
